item.title: R1-09-G2: Texas Rangers 5, Cincinnati Reds 7
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-10-31: the paper scorecard grid photo, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-09 Game 2 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Cincinnati Reds (seed 9) vs Texas Rangers (seed 24), home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 2 at Great American Ball Park. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every printed number; the two run-accounting settlements below are documented where the play log's run annotations and the card's printed RBI and wild pitch charges had to be read together. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Bucky Walters takes the win: Cincinnati took the lead for good in the Bottom 3 on Eric Davis's solo home run off Yu Darvish and never trailed, and Walters started and pitched 5.2 scoreless innings, leaving in the Top 6 with a 5-0 lead; Yu Darvish takes the loss as the starter charged with the Bottom 3 go-ahead run and the four Bottom 5 runs, leaving after Johnny Bench's 2-run single made it 5-0; Aroldis Chapman takes the save: he entered the Top 9 at 7-5 with the tying run at the plate and retired Corey Seager, Ian Kinsler and Ivan Rodriguez in order). Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Texas pitching allows 5 + 1 + 0 + 1 = 7 (Darvish, Jeff Zimmerman, Neftali Feliz, Jim Kern), and Cincinnati pitching allows 0 + 1 + 4 + 0 + 0 = 5 (Walters, Rob Dibble, Francisco Cordero, John Franco, Chapman). Bucky Walters was the story early: 5.2 innings, 3 hits, no runs, 1 walk, 3 strikeouts, stranding Josh Hamilton at third in the 2nd and Kinsler at second in the 6th. Cincinnati built the lead in layers: Davis's solo home run in the Bottom 3; a 4-run Bottom 5 keyed by Sparky Anderson's hit and run (graded paid off at +2.89, the inning's first run expectancy beaten by all four runs) in which Davis and Pete Rose singled, Joe Morgan walked, Frank Robinson hit a 2-run double and Bench a 2-run single, all off Darvish, with Ron Washington's call to leave the fatigued Darvish in for Bench graded backfired at -0.87; and a Bottom 6 run when pinch hitter Ted Kluszewski singled, Barry Larkin singled, and Rose doubled Kluszewski home for 6-0. Texas's only run through seven was Frank Howard's solo home run off Dibble in the Top 7. The Top 8 nearly flipped the game: Anderson's change to Cordero was graded backfired at -3.77, the worst single decision score of the tournament so far, matching the -3.77 Downs was graded at in R1-08 Games 4 and 5, as Seager doubled, Howard singled him in, and the inning's last three runs came across in Juan Gonzalez's plate appearance (settlement below) to make it 6-5; Franco got the last two outs of the inning. Cincinnati answered in the Bottom 8 with the Larkin run off Kern (settlement below) for 7-5, and Chapman closed it. Run-accounting settlement, Texas Top 8: the card prints Texas's RBI total at 4 (Howard 2, Gonzalez 2) against 5 runs, and charges Cordero with 1 wild pitch. The play log annotates Gonzalez's single as "(3 runs)" and never narrates a wild pitch. The log's base states settle it: after Howard's single the state was 2 out, bases 1st and 3rd, score TEX 2 (Seager home, Alex Rodriguez at 3rd, Howard at 1st); Hamilton's walk loaded the bases with Alex Rodriguez still at 3rd, so the wild pitch did not occur during Hamilton's plate appearance; Gonzalez's single then ends the play with the bases showing 1st only and the score TEX 5. The only consistent reading is that Cordero's wild pitch scored Alex Rodriguez during Gonzalez's at-bat, before the single (TEX 3, no RBI), and Gonzalez's single drove in Howard and Hamilton for his card-printed 2 RBI (TEX 5). It is the same settlement shape as the Key wild pitch in R1-08 Game 3: the log never narrates the wild pitch, the card charges it, and the card governs. Texas's printed RBI 4 plus the wild pitch run equals its 5 runs. Run-accounting, Cincinnati Bottom 8: there is no missing RBI and no settlement was needed beyond reading the card and the log's base states together; Cincinnati's printed RBI are Rose 1, Morgan 1, Robinson 2, Bench 2 and Davis 1, which sum to 7, matching the 7 runs. The Bottom 8 run is Larkin's: Kluszewski walked off Kern, Edd Roush pinch-ran and was thrown out at home on Larkin's double (the log's post-play state is 2 out, bases 2nd, Larkin at 2nd alone, which is why Larkin's printed RBI is 0 and the graded pinch runner note says the runner did not score), Rose walked, and Morgan's single to left scored Larkin for Morgan's 1 RBI and the 7-5 final margin. Wild pitch: the card charges Cordero with 1 wild pitch; a wild pitch is not a stored archive field and is noted here and in the settlement only. Errors: none, by either club, a clean game in the field for the second straight game. Sacrifices: none, and no sacrifice flies, for either club; the split SH and SF columns below are all zeros, log-proven (Ivan Rodriguez's Top 6 groundout advanced Kinsler to second but is a plain groundout, exactly as the card scores it). Hit batter: none. The scorecard grids print an HBP column for every pitcher on both clubs, all zeros, so HB 0 is carried for all nine pitchers and HBP 0 for every batter as card-sourced values, and the hit batter check runs on real data. Stolen bases and caught stealing, as printed: no runner stole a base all game (all nine steal sends across both managers were held, except one thrown out); Johnny Bench was caught stealing in the Bottom 4 after his walk, Cincinnati's only caught stealing, and Texas had none. Double plays grounded into, counted from the play log: Texas 1 (Alex Rodriguez, Top 1); Cincinnati 0 (Morgan's Bottom 3 forceout is not a GIDP). Substitutions: Kluszewski pinch-hit for Tony Perez in the Bottom 6 and stayed in as the designated hitter, singling in the 6th (and scoring on Rose's double) and walking in the 8th, 1 for 1 with a run; Edd Roush pinch-ran for Kluszewski in the Bottom 8 and was thrown out at home on Larkin's double; Roush never batted and the card gives him no batting line, so he is omitted from the batting table and carried in this recap only, the same handling as Alejandro Kirk in R1-08 Game 5. Availability held from Game 1 under the house outs convention: Eppa Rixey (8 outs in Game 1, capped at 3 outs) did not pitch, and Nolan Ryan (21 outs) and Noodles Hahn (10 outs), both unavailable, did not pitch. Game 3 availability, read off this game only (under 6 outs free, 6 to 8 outs capped at 3 outs, 9 or more outs unavailable for the next game): Darvish threw 13 outs and Walters 17 outs, so both are unavailable for Game 3; every reliever who appeared threw 5 outs or fewer (Zimmerman 5, Feliz 3, Kern 3, Dibble 4, Cordero 2, Franco 1, Chapman 3) and is free. The rotations turn over to each club's number 3 starter for Game 3 in any case, and the series shifts to Texas for Games 3 and 4 under the home pattern. Basepath aggression graded all night and almost never rewarded: twenty decisions total. Ron Washington made 7 (2 paid off, 5 backfired): three more steal sends (Top 1 Kinsler, Top 6 Kinsler, Top 7 Gonzalez) all held and all backfired, the Darvish leave-in backfired at -0.87, and the Jim Kern change backfired at -0.77 when the Bottom 8 insurance run scored; the Zimmerman change (+0.76) and the Feliz change (+0.73) paid off. Sparky Anderson made 13 (5 paid off, 5 backfired, 3 neutral): the Bottom 5 hit and run paid off at +2.89 and ignited the 4-run inning, the Dibble change paid off, the Kluszewski pinch hit paid off with the single that started the Bottom 6 run (the same call backfired in Game 1), the Bottom 8 steal send at 1 out graded paid off on the inning's run expectancy, and the Chapman closer call paid off; the Cordero change backfired at -3.77, four of his six steal sends backfired (Bench was thrown out on one of them), one steal send was neutral, and the Franco change and the Roush pinch runner graded neutral. Managers: Ron Washington (Texas) and Sparky Anderson (Cincinnati). Venue is Great American Ball Park. The series is tied 1-1.

item.title: R1-09-G1: Texas Rangers 7, Cincinnati Reds 4
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-10-31: the paper scorecard grid photo, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-09 Game 1 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. This game opens the series: Cincinnati Reds (seed 9) vs Texas Rangers (seed 24), home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 1 at Great American Ball Park. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every printed number. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Nolan Ryan takes the win: Texas took the lead for good in the Top 3 on Frank Howard's RBI single and Ryan pitched 7 innings; Noodles Hahn takes the loss as the starter charged with the go-ahead runs; Jeff Zimmerman takes the save: John Wetteland opened the Bottom 9 at 7-2 and gave up a walk and George Foster's 2-run home run without recording an out, and Zimmerman entered at 7-4 with the bases empty and pitched the full scoreless inning, a save under the lead-of-three-plus-one-inning condition, the same condition as Melancon's R1-08 Game 5 save). A clean game in the field: no errors, no sacrifices and no sacrifice flies for either club; Adrian Beltre's Top 4 RBI groundout is a plain groundout, not a sacrifice. Johnny Bench opened the scoring with a solo home run off Ryan in the Bottom 2. Texas answered in the Top 3: Corey Seager and Ian Kinsler hit back-to-back doubles to tie it, and Howard's 2-out single put Texas ahead to stay. Beltre's groundout scored Juan Gonzalez in the Top 4 for 3-1, and Gonzalez's solo home run off Eppa Rixey in the Top 6 made it 4-1; Gonzalez finished 4 for 4 with a double, the home run and 3 runs scored, and he was also caught stealing in the 2nd. Pete Rose's solo home run off Ryan in the Bottom 6 cut it to 4-2. Texas added two in the Top 8 off Francisco Cordero on doubles by Gonzalez and Rafael Palmeiro and a single by Beltre, and one more in the Top 9 off John Franco: Ian Kinsler was hit by a pitch, Ivan Rodriguez singled, Kinsler was retired on the bases on Alex Rodriguez's flyout, and Howard's single scored Ivan Rodriguez for 7-2. Ryan's line: 7.0 innings, 4 hits, 2 earned runs, 4 walks, 7 strikeouts, home runs allowed to Bench and Rose. The Bottom 9 nearly flipped it: Wetteland walked Joey Votto and Foster hit a 2-run home run, the closer call graded backfired at -1.77, before Zimmerman retired Ted Kluszewski, Eric Davis and Barry Larkin in order. Batters faced settlement: batters faced are counted from the play log. The log's ordering and the printed hit lines agree that Adrian Beltre's Top 8 single was hit off Cordero (the single is logged before Franco's entry, and the card charges Cordero with 3 hits, Beltre's among them, and Franco with 2), so Cordero is booked at 5 batters faced and Franco at 6; the club total is 41 either way and ties to Texas's 41 plate appearances. Wild pitch: the card charges Franco with 1 wild pitch; a wild pitch is not a stored archive field and is noted here only. Hit batter: Kinsler, hit by Franco in the Top 9, a card-sourced value carried in the tables below (Franco HB 1, every other pitcher 0), so the hit batter check runs on real data. Stolen bases and caught stealing, as printed: Kinsler stole second in the Top 1; Gonzalez was caught stealing in the Top 2; Frank Robinson was caught stealing in the Bottom 6 and Eric Davis was caught stealing in the Bottom 3 on the strikeout double play. Double plays grounded into: Hamilton, Top 5, Texas's only one; Cincinnati grounded into none (the Bottom 3 play was a strikeout with Davis thrown out stealing, not a GIDP). Substitution: Ted Kluszewski pinch-hit for Tony Perez in the Bottom 7 and stayed in as the DH, batting again in the Bottom 9; he finished 0 for 2. Basepath chaos graded all night: 18 decisions total. Ron Washington made 8 (2 paid off, 5 backfired, 1 neutral): both Top 1 hit and run calls backfired, his three steal sends produced two backfires and one neutral, but the Feliz change in the Bottom 8 and the Zimmerman change in the Bottom 9 both paid off; the Wetteland closer call backfired at -1.77. Sparky Anderson made 10 (4 paid off, 6 backfired): the Rixey, Dibble and Franco pitching changes paid off, the Cordero change backfired at -1.27 when Texas scored its 2 Top 8 runs, his Bottom 3 hit and run became a strikeout double play, the Kluszewski pinch hit backfired, and his four steal sends produced one paid off (Bottom 9, the Foster home run inning) against three held or thrown out. Game 2 availability under the house outs convention, read off this game only: Ryan threw 21 outs and Hahn 10 outs, so both would be unavailable for Game 2; Rixey threw 8 outs and would be capped at 3 outs; Wetteland threw 0 outs and is free; the rotations turn over to each club's number 2 starter for Game 2 in any case. Managers: Ron Washington (Texas) and Sparky Anderson (Cincinnati). Venue is Great American Ball Park. Texas leads the series 1-0.

item.title: R1-08-G5: Toronto Blue Jays 7, Pittsburgh Pirates 9
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-10-31: the paper scorecard grid photo, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-08 Game 5 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number with one documented exception, the hit batter settlement below. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Roy Face takes the win: Bob Friend left after 5 innings with a 5-4 lead, Toronto tied the game 5-5 in the Top 6 with Face pitching, and Pittsburgh's go-ahead 4 runs in the Bottom 6 scored while Face was still the pitcher of record, so Face is the winner; Scott Downs gave up all 4 of those Bottom 6 runs and takes the loss; Mark Melancon takes the save, entering the Top 9 with a 3-run lead at 9-6 and pitching the full inning under the lead-of-three-plus-one-inning condition). Toronto struck first: Alomar and Fernandez singled in the Top 1, Donaldson forced Fernandez, and Delgado's sacrifice fly made it 1-0. Pittsburgh answered at once in the Bottom 1: Wagner tripled, Clemente and Bonds walked, and Kiner hit a grand slam off Kevin Gausman for 4-1, Kiner's only RBI play of the day. Toronto kept coming: Moseby's 2-run home run off Friend in the Top 2 cut it to 4-3, and Moseby's RBI double in the Top 4 tied it 4-4; Moseby finished 3 for 3 with 3 RBI. Clemente's solo home run off Gausman in the Bottom 5 broke the tie at 5-4. The Top 6 tied it again: McGriff reached on Bonds's 2-base error in LF (Pittsburgh's only error) and Barfield singled him home, the run unearned, charged to Face's line as 1 R and 0 ER. The Bottom 6 decided the series: Cito Gaston went to Scott Downs and the change was graded backfired at -3.77 for the second straight game, as Stargell and Sanguillen singled (Sanguillen's drove in the go-ahead run), Murtaugh's hit and run was graded paid off at +2.74 when Leach tripled home another, Mazeroski's sacrifice fly scored Leach, and Wagner and McCutchen singled in a fourth run for 9-5; Gaston leaving Downs in during the inning was also graded backfired. Toronto got one back in the Top 7 on Delgado's RBI single off Dave Giusti (Delgado finished with 3 RBI) and threatened in the Top 8 against Kent Tekulve: Carter singled, Barfield walked, Moseby bunted them over, and Jose Bautista, pinch-hitting for Whitt, was hit by a pitch to load the bases, but Alomar grounded into an inning-ending double play. In the Top 9, Melancon gave up singles to Fernandez and Delgado (Delgado's scored Fernandez for 9-7) before striking out McGriff and getting Carter to ground out, closing the series; Murtaugh's closer call was graded backfired at -0.77 because of the run allowed, but the save stands. Hit batter settlement: the scorecard photo grid's pitchers-faced table prints Tekulve HBP 0, but the PDF box settles it the other way twice, listing "HBP: Jose Bautista" in the Toronto extras and "HBP by: Kent Tekulve 1" in the Pittsburgh extras, and the play log has Bautista hit by Tekulve's pitch in the Top 8; the game is therefore booked with HB 1 for Tekulve and HBP 1 for Bautista, and HB 0 for every other pitcher, all card-sourced values carried in the tables below so the homer, hit batter, and derived plate appearance checks run on real data. Downs's 2 wild pitches are printed on the scorecard; a wild pitch is not a stored archive field and is noted here only. Sacrifices, split as the card splits them: Delgado's sacrifice fly (Top 1) and Moseby's sacrifice bunt (Top 8) are Toronto's two; Mazeroski's sacrifice fly (Bottom 6) is Pittsburgh's one. Stolen bases: Fernandez stole second in the Top 9 and Wagner stole second in the Bottom 6, one each as printed. Double plays grounded into, counted from the play log: Toronto 4 (Delgado, Alomar, and Fernandez twice, in the Top 5 and Top 7; the card's extras list Fernandez once by name, the log shows both plays), Pittsburgh 1 (Leach, Bottom 7). Substitutions: Bautista pinch-hit for Whitt in the Top 8 and Alejandro Kirk replaced him at catcher in the Bottom 8 (Kirk did not bat); Arky Vaughan pinch-hit for Wagner in the Bottom 8, the platoon pinch hitters finishing the series at 1 paid off in 9 graded calls. Gaston's late changes to Eichhorn and Quantrill both graded paid off, holding Pittsburgh scoreless over the last two innings, and his Bautista pinch hit graded backfired at -1.13 on the hit by pitch outcome. Availability held from Game 4 under the house outs convention: Dave Stieb (unavailable, 17 outs in Game 4) and John Candelaria (unavailable, 16 outs in Game 4) did not pitch, and Pat Hentgen (6 outs in Game 4, capped at 3 outs) was not used. Graded decisions: Murtaugh 6 (the Bottom 6 hit and run paid off at +2.74; pitching changes Face neutral, Giusti backfired, Tekulve neutral, the Melancon closer call backfired at -0.77; the Vaughan pinch hit backfired). Gaston 7 (leaving Gausman in during the Bottom 5 paid off; the Downs change backfired at -3.77 and leaving Downs in backfired; the Eichhorn and Quantrill changes paid off, the Kirk defensive sub paid off, and the Bautista pinch hit backfired at -1.13). Managers: Danny Murtaugh (Pittsburgh) and Cito Gaston (Toronto). Venue is PNC Park. Pittsburgh wins the series 4-1, outscoring Toronto 45-25 across the five games. No series MVP is recorded yet; Joe rules on that next.

item.title: R1-08-G4: Pittsburgh Pirates 15, Toronto Blue Jays 5
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-10-30: a photo of the paper scorecard grid, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-08 Game 4 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (John Candelaria started for Pittsburgh, pitched into the 6th with the lead, and Pittsburgh never trailed after the Top 1, so he takes the win; Pat Hentgen was charged with 8 runs in 2 innings and took the loss; there is no save, Roy Face entered with a 7-run lead in the 6th and the final margin was 10). Pittsburgh scored in the Top 1 on Barry Bonds's RBI single. The Top 2 broke it open with 7 runs: Ralph Kiner led off with a home run, Manny Sanguillen singled, and Danny Murtaugh's hit and run (graded paid off at +5.39, the biggest decision score of the tournament so far, with six runs scoring after it) put runners at the corners on Tommy Leach's single; Honus Wagner singled in a run, Andrew McCutchen singled to load the bases, and Roberto Clemente reached on Carlos Delgado's 2-base error at 1B, scoring Leach and Wagner (2 runs, no RBI); Bonds followed with a 3-run home run for 8-0. Cito Gaston left a fatigued Hentgen in (graded paid off at +0.50), Willie Stargell struck out, Kiner reached on Joe Carter's 1-base error in LF, and the inning finally ended. Gaston's luck ran out in the Top 3: the Scott Downs pitching change was graded backfired at -3.77 as Leach and Bill Mazeroski singled and Wagner tripled both in, McCutchen's groundout scored Wagner (leaving Downs in was also graded backfired), and Dave Stieb, Toronto's rotation number 1 working in long relief, came in and gave up Clemente's home run at once (the change graded backfired as well) for 12-0. Toronto's only answer came in the Bottom 3: Ernie Whitt singled, Roberto Alomar reached on Leach's 1-base error at 3B, Tony Fernandez walked, and Josh Donaldson hit a grand slam, all four runs unearned. Carter's solo home run in the Bottom 4 was Toronto's last run and the only earned run charged to Candelaria, whose line stands as the card charges it: 5 runs, 1 earned. Stieb threw 5.2 innings of long relief from the 3rd, charged with 3 runs (Clemente's homer, and McCutchen's 2-run homer in the 8th). The Top 8 carried a streak note: Arky Vaughan pinch-hit for Wagner and walked (graded paid off at +2.00), ending Murtaugh's run of seven straight graded backfired platoon pinch hits across Games 1 to 4 (Paul Waner's Top 6 pinch hit in this game was the seventh); McCutchen's 2-run home run followed for 14-5. Kiner's second home run of the game, off Tom Henke in the Top 9 (the Henke change graded backfired), closed the scoring at 15-5. Earned-run notes, booked exactly as the card charges them: Candelaria 5 R and 1 ER (Toronto's 4-run 3rd was all unearned after Leach's error extended the inning, and Carter's solo homer in the 4th was the only earned run); Hentgen 8 R and 7 ER (the card charges 7 of the 8 earned, splitting the two runs that scored on Delgado's 2-base error in the 2nd). Pittsburgh's printed RBI total is 13 against 15 runs; the other 2 scored on Delgado's error (Leach and Wagner came home, Clemente reached), with no RBI, exactly as printed. No hit batters: the scorecard grid's pitching tables, in both the PDF and the paper scorecard photo, print HBP 0 for all eight pitchers, so HB 0 for all 8 pitchers and HBP 0 for all batters are card-sourced values carried in the tables below, and the homer, hit batter, and derived plate appearance checks run on real data. Sacrifices: the game's only two are Toronto sacrifice bunts to the pitcher, Alomar in the Bottom 5 and Lloyd Moseby in the Bottom 9; Ernie Whitt's Bottom 7 bunt was a fielder's choice (the lead runner was forced), not a sacrifice, and there were no sacrifice flies. Errors: Pittsburgh 1 (Leach, on Alomar in the Bottom 3); Toronto 2 (Delgado on Clemente and Carter on Kiner, both in the Top 2). The card also prints a caught stealing for Wagner (Top 5, after his single; the play log does not narrate it), carried in the tables as printed. Substitutions: Pittsburgh made two. Paul Waner pinch-hit for Clemente in the Top 6 and stayed in, and Arky Vaughan pinch-hit for Wagner in the Top 8 and stayed in. Toronto made no batting substitutions; Joe Carter started in LF and Lloyd Moseby in CF (George Bell and Devon White did not play), and Pittsburgh started Leach at 3B (Pie Traynor did not play). Graded decisions: Murtaugh 6 (hit and run paid off at +5.39; Waner pinch hit backfired, Vaughan pinch hit paid off at +2.00; pitching changes Face and Giusti paid off, Melancon neutral). Gaston 6 (leaving Hentgen in during the 2nd paid off at +0.50 and leaving Stieb in during the 8th was neutral; the Downs change backfired at -3.77, leaving Downs in backfired, the Stieb change backfired as Clemente homered, and the Henke change backfired as Kiner homered). Availability held from Game 3: Jimmy Key (unavailable, 18 outs in Game 3) and Babe Adams (unavailable, 27 outs in Game 3) both stayed out, correct. Managers: Danny Murtaugh (Pittsburgh) and Cito Gaston (Toronto). Venue is Rogers Centre.

item.title: R1-08-G3: Pittsburgh Pirates 7, Toronto Blue Jays 3
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-10-30: a photo of the paper scorecard grid, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-08 Game 3 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number subject to one scoring settlement, documented below. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Babe Adams pitched a complete game, the only Pittsburgh pitcher, and takes the win; Jimmy Key was charged with all 7 Pittsburgh runs and took the loss; Roberto Osuna, Duane Ward, and Tom Henke each threw one scoreless inning of relief; there is no save in a complete game win). Pittsburgh struck first: Roberto Clemente and Barry Bonds hit back-to-back home runs in the Top 1 for 2-0. Toronto answered in the Bottom 1: Tony Fernandez doubled, Carlos Delgado walked, and Fred McGriff doubled both in for 2-2. Clemente doubled in the Top 4, Willie Stargell walked, and Ralph Kiner's sacrifice fly made it 3-2. Toronto tied it again in the Bottom 4: McGriff doubled a second time and Jesse Barfield singled him in, 3-3. Tommy Leach tripled to open the Top 5 and Honus Wagner's groundout scored him for 4-3. The Top 6 settled the game: Clemente walked, Bonds singled him to 3rd, Stargell flew out, Clemente scored (on Key's wild pitch; see the settlement below), Kiner flew out to right, and Manny Sanguillen hit a 2-run home run for 7-3. Adams allowed nothing after the 4th; over the last five innings his only baserunners were Delgado's double in the 6th, Delgado's walk in the 8th, and Barfield's double in the 9th. The scoring settlement: Pittsburgh's printed RBI total is 6 against 7 runs. Kiner's line is 3 at-bats, 1 RBI, and one sacrifice fly, the Top 4 fly that scored Clemente, narrated as a sacrifice fly in the play log. In the Top 6 the play log attaches the score change (PIT 5) to Kiner's flyout line, but the scorecard counts that at-bat as a plain flyout (an at-bat, no sacrifice fly, no RBI) and charges Key with a wild pitch (WP 1, printed on the card). The only reading consistent with the card is that Clemente scored his Top 6 run on Key's wild pitch during Sanguillen's at-bat, before the 2-run homer; the play log does not narrate the wild pitch, the same way it does not narrate this game's two card-only caught stealings. The card governs: Kiner is booked exactly as printed (3 at-bats, sacrifice fly 1, RBI 1), the wild pitch stands charged to Key in this record (a wild pitch is not a stored archive field), no RBI is given for the wild pitch run, and Pittsburgh's team RBI total stands at 6. No hit batters: the scorecard grid's pitching tables, in both the PDF and the paper scorecard photo, print HBP 0 for all five pitchers, so HB 0 for all 5 pitchers and HBP 0 for all batters are card-sourced values carried in the tables below, and the homer, hit batter, and derived plate appearance checks run on real data. The caught stealings are card-only: the scorecard charges Roberto Alomar (Bottom 3, after his walk) and Tony Fernandez (Bottom 5, after his walk) with one each; the play log shows each runner gone by the end of the next at-bat without narrating the play, and the tables carry the card as printed. The game's only sacrifice is Kiner's Top 4 sacrifice fly; there were no sacrifice bunts. Neither club made an error. Substitutions: Pittsburgh only. Arky Vaughan pinch-hit for Wagner in the Top 7 and stayed in, and Paul Waner pinch-hit for Clemente in the Top 8 and stayed in. Toronto made no batting substitutions. Availability held from Game 2: Roy Halladay (unavailable, 18 outs in Game 2) and Wilbur Cooper (unavailable, 22 outs in Game 2) both stayed out, correct. Managers: Danny Murtaugh (Pittsburgh) and Cito Gaston (Toronto). Venue is Rogers Centre.

item.title: R1-08-G2: Toronto Blue Jays 6, Pittsburgh Pirates 5
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as the app scorecard PDF plus the full graded play-by-play text on 2026-10-30; official R1-08 Game 2 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Box score record: the two sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Duane Ward pitched a scoreless Bottom 8 with Toronto down 5-3 and was the pitcher of record when Toronto took the lead in the Top 9, taking the win; Mark Melancon, brought in as the closer for the Top 9, was charged with all three runs of the inning and took the loss; Tom Henke pitched a scoreless Bottom 9 with a 1-run lead for the save). Toronto led early: Roberto Alomar scored on Josh Donaldson's Top 1 sacrifice fly, and a Jose Bautista double, a George Bell single, and Jesse Barfield's two-run long single made it 3-0 in the 2nd. Pittsburgh answered in the Bottom 2 on Danny Murtaugh's hit and run: Pie Traynor doubled, Bill Mazeroski's groundout scored a run, and Honus Wagner tripled in another for 3-2. The Pirates tied it in the 3rd on Manny Sanguillen's sacrifice fly and went ahead on Traynor's RBI single, then made it 5-3 in the 4th on Wagner's double and Roberto Clemente's sacrifice fly. Wilbur Cooper held Toronto scoreless from the 3rd through the 7th and into the 8th, and Roy Face stranded two in the 8th around Donaldson's sacrifice bunt. Pittsburgh led 5-3 into the Top 9.
